captures.title: Update Forge and Mirror for the new build_check contract
captures.note:
build_check's output contract changed and landed on ourliberty-graph main (f847ae9, 2026-07-20). The droplet pulls it hourly, so Forge and Mirror instructions are now stale and describe a verdict that no longer exists.

WHAT CHANGED: build_check used to band a TF-IDF cosine score into STRONG / POSSIBLE / NONE and tell the builder whether reuse existed. It no longer emits any verdict. It now prints the top 3 catalogued candidates (id, profile, full capability statement, location) and asks the reader to judge each as REUSE (same job, extend it), ADAPT (same problem at a different altitude or shape, pattern transfers but work remains), or NONE (build net-new).

WHY: cosine magnitude tracks term density and document length, not relevance. Measured: the 0.25 band passed only 14 of 30 in-domain eval cases that the same ranking placed at rank 1 (29/30), and 0 of 13 cross-product cases. It was discarding more than half the matches it had correctly found. Retrieval ranks well but cannot judge; the reader is an agent that can.

CHANGE 1 — agents/forge/CLAUDE.md, the preflight consult step (currently near line 47-50). It says: "It returns a SHELF verdict ... If the verdict is STRONG, your plan should reuse/extend the named component rather than reimplement it." Replace that with the judgment contract above: you receive candidates, you decide REUSE/ADAPT/NONE and record your call and reasoning in preflight_summary. Keep the existing fail-safe wording ("build-check skipped" on error, never block) and the skip-for-trivial-edits rule exactly as they are.

CHANGE 2 — Mirror Lens I wording. It still refers to the librarian as "v1 brittle" and cites the old score bands. Replace with the same judgment contract. There is a pre-existing card for this wording fix (task_9e589a09); fold it in.

GUIDANCE FOR BOTH: judge on substance, not shared vocabulary. Cross-altitude matches (a workflow card answering a schema need) are normal and frequently correct. "None of these fit" is a legitimate, expected outcome, not a failure.

REFERENCE: ourliberty-graph docs/build-loop.md carries the full contract and the measurement behind it. Do not reintroduce a score threshold.

captures.title: Thirteen writers do unlocked read-modify-write on build-sequence files
captures.note: STANDING HAZARD, broader than the #1052 arc that surfaced it. Build-sequence JSON files under ~/agents/blackboard/build-sequences/ are read-modify-written by THIRTEEN separate scripts, none of which takes a lock: beacon_approval_handler, build_sequence_advancer, build_sequence_kickoff, dashboard_api, heal_completed_sequence_mission_reconcile, heal_forge_wip_only_redispatch, heal_pipeline_stall, launch_dedup_gc, launch_queue_drain, outbox_notifier, pr_terminal_fanout, sequence_shortcut_helpers, system_state_log. Each reads the whole file, mutates a field or appends an audit entry, and atomically replaces it. Atomic replace makes each WRITE safe; it does nothing about the read-modify-write WINDOW, so when two of these overlap the later write silently discards the earlier one. Demonstrated concretely for the heal_pipeline_stall + outbox_notifier pair: an audit entry written by one vanishes entirely when the other replaces the file from a snapshot read moments earlier. The consequence is not cosmetic. These audit entries are a CONTROL CHANNEL, not just a log. dag-preflight-sync-lag-detected is what arms heal_pipeline_stall Check 12; dag-preflight-revision-routed is what arms Check 9; dag-preflight-pass-kickoff is what proves a preflight round closed. Losing one to a lost update disarms the backstop that watches a stalled build, which returns the system to the exact silent-stall failure #1052 was written to end. Also at risk: step status transitions and current_steps, i.e. two writers could disagree about which step is live. THE FIX: migrate all thirteen writers to atomic_io.locked_update, which is the repo's established advisory-lock helper and is already used for ledgers. Its docstring is explicit that the guarantee holds ONLY if EVERY writer of a path goes through it, so all writers of a given file must be migrated TOGETHER. That is why this is a project and not a patch, and why a partial migration is worse than none in one specific sense: it protects one pair while reading like a closed hole. locked_update is fail-open by design (runs unserialized rather than wedging when the lock cannot be taken), so the migration cannot deadlock a daemon. PRIORITY: not urgent. The window is sub-millisecond per write and the pair-specific trigger needs a sync-lag incident, which agent-core #1053 made much rarer. But it is a standing correctness hazard on shared state that will outlive the sync-lag arc, and the cost only grows as more writers are added. FOUR CARD TYPES, FOUR DIFFERENT BROKEN APPROVES, ONE ROOT CAUSE:
1. Session-less mirror-review escalate (mirror-review-*): Approve dispatches a fresh Forge revision against code that is already correct. RSDPM #166 (2026-07-30) — Mirror escalated a legitimate SCOPE question (the PR deliberately did not do its brief, with evidence the brief's premise was false); Approve would have sent Forge to make the exact change the PR argues causes false DRIFT. Also agent-core #884, RSDPM #111.
2. Deep-review hold (deep-review-hold-*): Approve posts the token and never merges, re-posting every 60s forever. RSDPM #157, #160, #161, #165 all needed a manual merge after stamping. See cap-deep-review-hold-approve-posts-the-token-but-nev-2d25.
3. Promoted/orphaned (unreg-approval-*): Approve is a total no-op — no dispatch, no merge, no error. agent-core #1058. agent-core PR #1060 fixes only this one variant and is still OPEN.
4. Larry-alert promotions: #1060 leaves them out of scope and NEITHER button works. See cap-larry-alert-promotions-1060-leaves-them-out-of-s-aaf0.

PROBLEM: approval cards go stale because nothing re-checks their premise. Today's only clearing signals answer 'did Beacon already resolve this?' (task_id in history, not pending) or 'did a PR for this task_id merge/close?' (task_terminal_state -> MERGED/CLOSED). A card whose premise is a fact about live state — a DB row, a file's contents, a code behavior — probes UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN means keep forever. On 2026-07-29, 6 of 8 cards on the tab did not need a human.

THIS SLICE — SCHEMA + EVALUATOR ONLY. No wiring into any healer, no UI.
1. Optional 'freshness_probe' on an approval's dispatch_payload: a deterministic, machine-checkable predicate whose FALSITY means the ask is moot.
2. Kinds to support: pr_state (reuse task_terminal_state), file_contains / file_lacks (git show at origin/main, repo+ref+path), json_path (a config key), sql (read-only). Leave 'shell' OUT of this slice.

LOAD-BEARING SEMANTICS (the whole point — get these in the tests):
  TRUE => premise still holds => keep the card.
  FALSE => premise dead => the card is moot.
  ERROR / timeout / unparseable / unknown kind => INDETERMINATE, which callers MUST treat as KEEP.

Its outbox envelope reads exit_code=-1, result='TIMEOUT after 600s', duration_sec=None. No APPROVAL_REQUEST was ever emitted, so no card was ever created. The capture is still state=parked, promoted_to=None — BYTE-IDENTICAL ON THE BOARD TO A CARD NOBODY EVER DELEGATED. One Telegram alert fired at 01:21:54Z and that was the entire signal.

IT WAS NOT AN OUTLIER — IT WAS THE TREND HITTING THE WALL. Delegation durations that night: 4b31 186s -> PR #1063; d5d1 251s -> PR #159 merged; fd54 336s -> PR #1058 merged; 71d1 536s -> dispatched; 8bb3 KILLED at 600s. 71d1 survived by 64 seconds. The wall is real and close.

THREE DISTINCT GAPS — a preflight should scope which are worth closing:

1. NOTHING RETRIES. No healer re-drives a failed delegation; no requeue; no backoff. Verified by grep across scripts/heal_*.py. The work is simply gone.

2. NOTHING SURFACES IT. heal_missions_card_gc:1230 states the design intent — 'a delegate that never opened a PR probes UNKNOWN and MUST surface as still-open, never silently close.' It does stay open. But 'open' RENDERS AS parked, which is the same pixel as never-touched. dashboard_api already carries delegated_at / approval_id on the delegate response (dashboard_api.py:1028, 1256, 8064 'delegated_at stays honest') — the data to distinguish the two states EXISTS and the board does not use it. Cheapest thread.

3. duration_sec=None ON A 600s TIMEOUT IS A LIE WAITING TO BE BELIEVED. outbox_notifier's definitive-non-run classifier (~:3043, :3100) recognizes 'spawn-failure' as exit_code==-1 AND duration None-or-under-2s AND an 'all retries exhausted' signal. A timeout satisfies the first TWO. Today it is saved only by the third predicate (our text says 'TIMEOUT after 600s', not 'retries exhausted') — so a task that ran ten full minutes is one string away from being classified as a worker that never spawned. Record the real elapsed time.

DO NOT just raise the timeout. 600s is a reasonable ceiling; the parent capture was genuinely too big to scope (it is being split into 3 slices: ...582f, ...9902, ...2616). Raising the wall hides the size problem instead of surfacing it. If anything, the right move is the opposite — tell the operator a delegation died and why, so an oversized card gets split rather than silently retried into the same wall.

REVIEW: needed if it changes retry or dispatch behavior — a retry loop on a 10-minute agent spawn is real money, and 'it silently did nothing' is the failure class this whole capture is about.

captures.note:
REPLACES cap-larry-alert-promotions-1060-leaves-them-out-of-s-aaf0 (dropped 2026-07-30, no reason recorded — believed accidental; adjacent card, similar name). ALSO SUPERSEDES cap-heal-unregistered-approval-mints-permanent-cards-b921 — drop that one, it predates #1060 and half its content is now obsolete.

WHAT #1060 ALREADY FIXES (merged 85732bec, 02:29Z — do NOT rebuild): three deterministic legs — the promoter stamps promoted_source + a fail-closed recheck_target; Approve on a coordinate-carrying card dispatches a real Mirror re-review; heal_stale_escalation_recheck widened so those cards retire on MERGED/CLOSED/superseded. It closes the 21:55Z incident where Approve wrote a ledger row, cleared the card, and executed nothing.

THE RESIDUE IS NAMED IN #1060's OWN BODY, verbatim: 'Larry-alert promotions never carry a coordinate and stay out of scope.'

That is EXACTLY the class that reached Larry on 2026-07-29 — every one a promoted larry-alert, not a for-Larry mirror-review: unreg-approval-9061de515dce (unrouted PR#1049), -3283b7a9b651 (unrouted PR#1053), -cfd444ed29ee (RSDPM migration 0033 — false 8 min before he saw it), -67747fb0837e (the unrouted nag for PR#1060 ITSELF), and -953eb339a46c (same nag, PR#1062). Five in one day.

AFTER #1060 THIS CLASS HAS NO WORKING EXIT:
  - Approve 400s before the read_at claim (correct — no silent clear), so the card stays visible and unactionable.
  - Reject: #1060 lists it as unchanged residue (paid Beacon no-op, RSDPM #59 class). NOTE: observed 2026-07-30 01:05Z, a dashboard SOFT reject on -67747fb0837e resolved cleanly with 'no Mirror review dispatched, no in-flight work aborted' — so a soft-reject path may already work. Preflight should establish which reject path the tab actually invokes before assuming cost.
  - The recheck ladder is coordinate-gated, so these never auto-retire.
A card that says in its own summary 'could not be parsed into two options — needs triage' and has no working verb is pure tab debt. Three of the four sat through 6 reminder rounds.

BUILD (pick in preflight):
(a) Do not promote a larry-alert the promoter cannot parse into two real options. A card that cannot state its own choices is TRIAGE, not a decision — route it somewhere that is not the Approvals tab.
(b) If promoted, inherit the source alert's dedup/cooldown identity so the card retires when the alert does. Today the alert de-dups and cools down; the card it spawned outlives it forever.
(c) CHEAPEST THREAD: bare_approvable=False is ALREADY stamped on every one (heal_unregistered_approval.py:717/889/1210) and read ONLY by beacon_approval_handler.py:634, purely to stop a bare Telegram 'approve' hitting the wrong card. The record ALREADY KNOWS these are not binary decisions. Nothing acts on it.

DO NOT 'fix the detector'. heal_pipeline_stall.check_unrouted_open_prs / heal-unrouted-owner-pr-nudge-001 works as designed: it exists to catch 'a clean unrouted PR the owner forgot to label', deliberately nudge-only, preserving Larry's 2026-07-11 label opt-in (PR_UNROUTED_MIN_AGE_MIN=60). It cannot tell 'forgot' from 'deliberately holding for /code-review high' because nothing records that intent. The alert is not the bug; the PROMOTION is.

ADJACENT: the freshness slices (...582f / ...9902 / ...2616) cover cards whose PREMISE goes stale. This covers cards that were never answerable.

REVIEW: needed — it changes what reaches the Approvals tab, and a wrong filter drops a real decision while looking exactly like a working tab.

briefing.what: Some alert cards land in your approval list that you can't actually act on — pressing Approve or Reject does nothing, so they just sit there.
briefing.why: You got five of these in a single day and most lingered through six reminder rounds, cluttering your list and burying the real decisions that need you.
briefing.suggest: Worth fixing, but move carefully — first confirm exactly how the buttons behave today, then keep these unanswerable items out of your list rather than risking a change that hides a real decision.

captures.risk_note: This touches something hard to undo (data, deploys, money, or outside contact) — worth a careful look before acting.
